assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines the physiology of GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and led to therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and renal outcome benefits. Rare combination of basic physiology, mechanism and very broad clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 actions and biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2), Holst (GLP-1 as the incretin in humans, secretion and physiology) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry and identification of the active GLP-1 form) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's drug-development role is major but industrial, and credit between academic discovery and drug design is contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and multiple approved drugs with outcome-trial evidence; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the identification of active GLP-1 among Mojsov, Habener and others; Habener is not credited in this entry and I cannot verify the dispute details.
Whether the committee prefers to honor the drug-development step (Knudsen) over the physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies established a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with several approved products and wide conceptual influence on cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB costimulation) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs, preclinical proof) are central. Rosenberg contributed to adoptive cell therapy and early clinical work; the original CAR concept (Eshhar, Gross) is not in the credited names, which complicates fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Approved products, years of follow-up and independent replication; long-term durability, toxicity and solid-tumor limits remain, but the core discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Original chimeric receptor concept credit falls outside the supplied names.
Choice between June, Sadelain and Rosenberg for a three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: VLP-based HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other HPV-related cancers; a clear, clinically proven prevention of human cancer with global public health impact and strong originality in the VLP concept.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine development, with the late Jian Zhou) are a natural trio; the supplied names do not include Zhou, who is deceased, which is an attribution gap but not obstructive.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data show sharp reductions in cervical precancer and cancer; confirmation is extensive and independent. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Frazer, Zhou, Lowy and Schiller, and the role of other VLP groups; I have not independently verified the details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of intracellular signaling from the ER to the nucleus, a basic mechanism of cellular quality control with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and aging. Original, clear and conceptually foundational.
assessment.attribution: Mori (HAC1/IRE1 pathway, identification of UPR elements) and Walter (IRE1 splicing mechanism, PERK, ISRIB) have clearly decisive complementary contributions in a fair two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation in yeast and mammals; therapeutic translation (ISRIB, other modulators) is still emerging, but the discovery stands on basic science.
uncertainties: Possible inclusion of other contributors (e.g., Ron, Kaufman, Schekman) is not supported by the supplied names.
Clinical relevance is mostly indirect so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed neuroscience by allowing causal, cell-type-specific control of activity; the discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use in neurons is widely used across biology, with early clinical vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterization), Bamberg (early work), Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal deployment), Miesenboeck (earlier genetically targeted photoactivation). Three-laureate limit makes allocation hard; this selection prioritizes the molecular discovery and the key neuronal application.
assessment.maturity: Extensively replicated and a standard tool for over a decade; maturity strong, though some see it as technology rather than discovery of a disease mechanism.
uncertainties: Contested priority between Boyden and Deisseroth, and weight of Bamberg and Miesenboeck.
Fit with the medicine mandate for a tool versus a therapy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a chronic manageable one and proved the principle of targeted kinase inhibition against an oncogenic driver; very high clinical and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development and kinase inhibitor program), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) are credible. Rowley and Nowell/Hungerford, Witte and Baltimore on BCR-ABL itself are not in the supplied names; Zimmermann, a chemist, also played a role.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of follow-up and survival data; fully mature, with Lasker recognition already given. Possible concern that the field has moved on, though recognition remains valid.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the drug or the BCR-ABL discovery lineage whose contributors are partly outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishment of Lgr5 stem cell-derived self-organizing organoids enabled long-term culture of adult epithelia and patient-derived disease models, now broadly used in disease modeling, drug testing and regenerative research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the conceptual and intellectual driver (Lgr5 stem cell identification, Wnt-based culture), with Sato as the first author of the key organoid methods; a two-person configuration is clean, though Clevers alone might be considered.
assessment.maturity: Widespread adoption and replication, but clinical impact is still moderate and the field is evolving; some may view recognition as slightly early.
uncertainties: Relationship to earlier 3D culture and embryonic stem cell organoid work not covered by the supplied names.
Degree of clinical translation to date.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 identified the first regulator of apoptosis that acts by survival rather than proliferation, defining a new oncogene class and leading to BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax) with real clinical benefit in CLL and other leukemias.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams (BCL-2 family biology and its role in lymphoma and apoptosis control) and Vaux (BCL-2 as a cell death inhibitor in lymphoma models) are central; Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto (BCL-2 cloning in the t(14;18) translocation) as well as Strasser's contributions complicate allocation. I cannot confirm exact priority details.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic confirmation and approved therapy provide strong maturity; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Key early contributors (Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer) are outside or deceased and not on the supplied list.
Drug-development credit sits with other groups.
